text_plugin_synopsis: File manager plugin. Secure read-only previewer for Markdown files
p_languages_all_supported_for_readme: The current README.md supports the following languages
p_introduction: Markdown Previewer is a previewer plugin for the AutoJs6 file manager. Once enabled, every Markdown file in the file manager gains a `Markdown Previewer` action in its overflow menu. Tap it to read the document nicely rendered, like a web page, instead of a wall of raw source text.
p_introduction_secure: The plugin does one thing and does it safely: read-only rendering. The viewer never executes scripts, can only read files temporarily authorized by the host, and renders everything in its own screen. It does not modify AutoJs6 itself and has no effect on the script runtime.
highlights: Read rendered Markdown documents right inside the AutoJs6 file manager, with no file exports and no third-party reader apps.
Tables, task lists, strikethrough, automatic links, heading anchors, and in-document images work out of the box, covering common GitHub-style writing.
Five built-in previewer themes: GitHub (Auto), GitHub Light, GitHub Dark, Paper, and Sepia. The auto theme follows the system light/dark mode.
Import a custom CSS file to build your own reading style. It layers on top of the built-in styling and can be cleared with one tap.
Immersive fullscreen mode with an optional `Start in fullscreen mode` preference. The back button leaves fullscreen first instead of closing the page.
Pinch to zoom, manual refresh, horizontally scrollable tables, and automatic BOM-based detection of UTF-8 / UTF-16 / UTF-32 encodings.
A read-only security sandbox: no JavaScript execution, no disk caches, and no access to any data beyond the files authorized by the host.
p_usage_prerequisites: Before starting, confirm the following requirements
p_usage_steps_intro: It takes 4 steps from installation to your first rendered document
usage_steps: Download and install the plugin APK. The plugin has no launcher icon; after installation it is managed entirely by AutoJs6.
Open AutoJs6, enter the `Plugin center`, locate `Markdown Previewer`, and enable it.
In the AutoJs6 file manager, locate any Markdown file (such as `README.md`) and open its overflow menu.
Select `Markdown Previewer`. The document opens rendered in a dedicated viewer.
p_usage_viewer_tips: Inside the viewer, the top-right menu offers `Refresh`, `Previewer theme`, `Import custom CSS`, `Fullscreen mode`, and `Settings`, where `Settings` provides the `Start in fullscreen mode` switch. http/https links in the document open in the system browser, while heading anchor links jump within the viewer. Explorer Action v2 supports both the primary previewer button and the overflow menu for a single file, using temporary read grants for the document and its parent directory. AutoJs6 build 5269 or later is required.
p_supported_formats: The plugin recognizes the following filename extensions
p_supported_formats_note: Files whose extension is not listed but whose MIME type is `text/markdown` or `text/x-markdown` can be viewed as well. A single document may be at most {{ limit_markdown_size }}; oversized files produce a clear message instead of a truncated rendering.

faq.question: The file menu does not show `Markdown Previewer`?
faq.answer: Check the following in order: the AutoJs6 version code is at least {{ required_host_build }} (version 6.8.0 or later qualifies); the plugin is enabled in the `Plugin center`; and the file extension is in the supported list. If any of the three fails, the menu action will not appear.

faq.question: Opening fails with `Cannot read the Markdown file`?
faq.answer: Common causes: the file was moved, renamed, or deleted at the moment of opening; the file exceeds {{ limit_markdown_size }}; or the call did not come from the AutoJs6 file manager. For security reasons the plugin rejects invocations from any other source.

faq.question: Why are images in the document not shown?
faq.answer: The viewer loads only three kinds of images: local images referenced by relative paths within the document directory (including subdirectories), inline `data:` images, and public `https` images. Plain `http` images and private or reserved network addresses are blocked by the security policy.

faq.question: Can it display HTML files?
faq.answer: No. This plugin focuses on Markdown. HTML viewing is provided by the separate HTML Previewer plugin; see the links below.

faq.question: How does custom CSS work?
faq.answer: Choose `Import custom CSS` from the menu and pick a stylesheet no larger than {{ limit_custom_css_size }}. The theme switches to `Custom CSS` automatically. The stylesheet layers on top of the base styling, so you only write the rules you want to override. Choose `Clear custom CSS` to return to `GitHub (Auto)`.

faq.question: How does syntax highlighting work, and why are Mermaid and math formulas not rendered?
faq.answer: Syntax highlighting is generated during Markdown rendering for recognized code languages and does not require JavaScript. Mermaid and math formulas still depend on client-side scripts, so they are not rendered because the viewer keeps JavaScript disabled.

p_security_intro: The viewer is built on a deny-by-default principle. All of the following measures are always on and cannot be disabled
security_points: Rendered output is sanitized against an allowlist: scripts, forms, iframes, inline event handlers, and other dangerous content are removed, and JavaScript stays disabled throughout.
The WebView runs with storage, cookies, form saving, and filesystem access turned off. The rendered result lives only in memory and is destroyed when the page closes.
The plugin reads the selected file and its directory solely through temporary content URIs granted by the host. It receives no filesystem paths and requests no additional runtime permissions.

CSP plus request interception restrict resource loading twice over: only built-in stylesheets, resources inside the document directory, `data:` images, and `https` images pass; every other request is rejected.
Remote images are filtered against private and reserved addresses (anti-SSRF) and loaded with a no-referrer policy; external links can only open in the system browser.
Inputs are bounded: Markdown up to {{ limit_markdown_size }}, custom CSS up to {{ limit_custom_css_size }}, with display name and path lengths limited as well.

p_resource_layout: `strings.xml` localizes plugin metadata and the viewer UI, while `plugin_instruction.md` provides the usage instructions shown by the host. All README and CHANGELOG files are generated from JSON sources by `.python/generate_markdown.py`: to change the docs, edit the `lang_*.json` files under `.readme` and `.changelog` and rerun the script instead of editing the generated Markdown files
